case_studies.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models
case_studies.abstract: A prominent research direction in mechanistic interpretability is learning sparse circuits over LLM components to reveal how they jointly produce model behavior. However, raw neurons are polysemantic, making learned circuits hard to interpret. Sparse autoencoder (SAE) features alleviate this, but their high dimensionality makes existing intervention-based circuit learning methods computationally prohibitive. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of interpreting large language models by building a scalable circuit-learning approach called CircuitLasso, which results in structurally accurate circuits. The approach helps reveal how language model components jointly produce model behavior. It is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: When Agent Automation Becomes Profitable: Quantifying and Insuring Autonomous AI Risk through Trace-Economic Underwriting
case_studies.abstract: AI agents can now take irreversible actions in operational systems, but agent-caused losses are still not clearly assigned, priced, or transferred. Providers often disclaim consequential damages, users are left with uncompensated losses, and default human review limits the efficiency gains of automation. We ask when autonomous AI deployment can become economically acceptable despite failure risk. Our answer is to quantify risk at the customer-task-trace episode level and transfer it through insurance. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of unassigned and uncompensated losses caused by autonomous AI agents in operational systems by quantifying risk and transferring it through insurance. The researchers built a system to quantify risk at the customer-task-trace episode level. The result is that automation is economically acceptable when its expected benefit exceeds the premium, control cost, and remaining risk.

case_studies.summary: TokenPilot solves the problem of high inference costs in LLM agents by managing context accumulation, the researchers built a dual-granularity context management framework, and the result is a more efficient use of cache memory. This framework helps reduce inference costs in long-horizon sessions. The research focuses on improving LLM agent performance.

case_studies.title: ARB4WM: An Adversarial Robustness Benchmark for World Models in Continuous Control
case_studies.abstract: World models are widely used in robotic and agentic engineering control systems due to their ability to learn latent dynamics for planning and decision-making. As these systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical settings, understanding their robustness under adversarial conditions has become essential. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating the robustness of world models in robotic and agentic engineering control systems under adversarial conditions. The result provides a benchmark for pre-deployment risk assessment of these systems.

case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often fail when answering requires identifying a small but decisive piece of evidence within a long or complex context, such as a single line in a tool trace or a subtle detail in an image. However, generating high-utility synthetic data often carries the risk of memorizing and regurgitating private information from the training corpus. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of synthetic data potentially disclosing private information from its training corpus by creating a framework to detect and explain such disclosures. The result is a tool that helps ensure synthetic data is privacy-preserving.

case_studies.title: KVEraser: Learning to Steer KV Cache for Efficient Localized Context Erasing

This issue arises naturally in long-context LLM applications, where stale retrieved facts, incorrect tool observations, retracted user preferences, or harmful prompt injections may be identified only after prefill. case_studies.abstract: Sparse reward reinforcement learning (RL) has become a standard tool for improving LLM reasoning, but its success depends critically on the coverage present in the base model. In practice, models are often primed for RL through \emph{mid-training} on curated reasoning traces that teach useful primitive skills such as decomposition, verification, or self-correction. case_studies.title: Tangram: Hiding GPU Heterogeneity for Efficient LLM Parallelization

case_studies.summary: Tangram solves the problem of efficient parallelization of large language models in heterogeneous GPU clusters by hiding GPU heterogeneity, the researchers built a system to make search tractable in these clusters, and the result is more efficient LLM parallelization. This system enables the use of existing heterogeneous GPU clusters without omitting types of parallelism or memory-saving techniques. It allows for better parallelization plans in these environments.
